title: Strong claim filed nineteen months late
narrative: I only just found out I could claim for this. It was a clear-cut case, they admitted it was their fault at the time.

documents.content:
BOOKING BR3312 — Passenger: Q. MENSAH (adult)
Carrier: Boreal Rift (BR)
BR150  YYZ 04 Feb 2025 18:20  ->  LHR 05 Feb 2025 06:30
Great-circle distance YYZ-LHR: 5,720 km.
Status: CONFIRMED.

From: ops@borealrift.example
Sent: 04 Feb 2025 12:00 UTC
Subject: BR150 cancelled

BR150 this evening is cancelled. We are sorry; this was caused by a fault on our aircraft and no replacement is available tonight.

BOREAL RIFT OPS LOG — BR150 / 04FEB2025
Status: CANCELLED
Cause code: TECH-UNSCH
Cause text: Nose gear steering fault found by BR line maintenance at YYZ. No manufacturer directive. BR accepts this as within its control.
No weather, no ATC restriction.

Claim prepared for filing with Boreal Rift on 12 Sep 2026.
Scheduled departure of the first affected segment: 04 Feb 2025 18:20.
Elapsed between scheduled departure and filing: 19 months and 8 days.
CHECK-IN CONFIRMATION BR150 04FEB2025 — MENSAH/Q — accepted for travel 16:44Z, seat 44J. Flight subsequently cancelled.

derivation: S1.2(c) a claim must be filed within 18 months of the scheduled departure of the first affected segment
Scheduled departure 04 Feb 2025, filing 12 Sep 2026, an elapsed 19 months and 8 days
S1.3 a claim failing any limb of S1.2 is out of scope and receives no compensation and no duty of care
The merits are strong and the carrier admits fault, and none of that survives S1.3
S2 and S3 are reached in the analysis but cannot rescue an out-of-scope claim
